summary: All 5 target claims from brief.md were critiqued side-by-side against counter-claims.json. 2 original claims held essentially unchanged (BFCL multi-turn tool-use collapse; NVIDIA SLM thesis as an unrebutted industry position, now with an explicit easier-benchmark scope caveat). 1 tension was resolved in the original brief's favor via a credible mechanistic reconciliation (SWRV/CoCoS gains vs. process-verification harm -- explained by trained-verifier vs. free-form self-critique, upgraded from unresolved to resolved). 3 original claims/framings did not survive scrutiny and were downgraded: the 350M-parameter ToolBench result (its evaluation instrument is independently documented as unreliable), Devstral's 'SOTA among open code-agent models' framing (superseded within the same timeframe, though the raw 53.6% figure itself stands as an unrepeated vendor-only number), and the brief's unqualified framing of RAG as 'one of the better-evidenced compensators' (a real-production WeChat study shows the oracle-RAG precondition is load-bearing, not cosmetic -- non-oracle RAG can actively harm via context pollution). Two counter-claims were themselves found to over-reach and were pushed back on: treating Devstral's supersession as contradiction rather than expiration, and treating the orchestrator-driven small-multi-agent finding as directly refuting rather than merely qualifying the NVIDIA thesis. One item remains genuinely unresolved on both sides: live multi-small-model orchestration vs. single-model distillation as the more effective architecture.
